1	# Business Requirements Document: Credit Control
2	
3	| | |
4	|---|---|
5	| Prepared for | Finance Director |
6	| Prepared by | Business Analyst, Finance |
7	| Version | 1.0 (draft for sign-off) |
8	| Status | For review by Finance, Sales and IT |
9	
10	## 1. Purpose
11	
12	This document sets out what the business needs from a credit control capability in our ERP system. Today credit control lives in a spreadsheet and in the head of our credit controller. The board has asked that it move into the ERP, so that the same rules are applied to every customer every time, so that sales staff and customers cannot get around them, and so that our auditors can see what was decided, by whom and when.
13	
14	The document describes the business behaviour we want. It does not say how the software should be built.
15	
16	## 2. Background
17	
18	We are a wholesale distributor with about 900 trade customers on account. Customers are billed in several currencies. Orders reach us in four main ways: entered by our sales office, placed by customers through our web shop, sent to us electronically by larger customers, and raised automatically from standing monthly orders.
19	
20	Last financial year our bad debt write-offs were well above what the board considers acceptable. A review found the main causes were:
21	
22	- Customers kept being supplied after they had stopped paying, because the "stop list" was a spreadsheet that the sales office and the web shop did not check.
23	- Credit limits were set once when the account was opened and rarely looked at again.
24	- Reminder letters were sent irregularly, depending on how busy the credit controller was.
25	- We charged no interest or late fees, so slow payers had no reason to pay on time.
26	- Write-offs were posted inconsistently, and at year end the auditors had trouble matching the sales ledger to the general ledger and to the decisions behind each write-off.
27	
28	We already use the ERP for sales orders, invoicing, customer accounts, statements and the general ledger, so the credit control work should sit there too.
29	
30	## 3. Stakeholders
31	
32	| Stakeholder | Interest |
33	|---|---|
34	| Finance Director (sponsor) | Lower bad debt, consistent control, a clean audit. |
35	| Maria, Credit Controller | Runs credit control day to day: reviews, stops, reminders, charges, write-offs. |
36	| Deputy Credit Controller | Covers for Maria with the same authority. |
37	| Financial Accountant | Month-end close; the ledger must agree with customer accounts. |
38	| Sales Manager and sales reps | Need to know which of their customers are on stop or on watch; must not be able to override it. |
39	| Sales office / order entry | Must be stopped from processing orders for customers on stop. |
40	| Customers | See their own reminders, interest and fees; receive reminder letters by email. |
41	| External auditors | Need a trail of credit decisions, charges and write-offs. |
42	| IT / system administrator | Installs and configures the change on our live system. |
43	
44	## 4. Scope
45	
46	### 4.1 In scope
47	
48	1. Periodic credit reviews of customers, recording the outcome, notes and the next review date.
49	2. Putting customers "on stop" (also called "on hold" or "frozen") and taking them off stop.
50	3. A softer "watch" status for customers we are worried about but still supply.
51	4. Overdue reminder letters ("chasers", "dunning letters") in escalating stages, sent by email.
52	5. Interest and/or late fees on overdue balances, charged at month end.
53	6. Writing off bad debts.
54	7. A report of customers due a credit review and customers over their credit limit.
55	8. Sales reps seeing only their own customers' credit information.
56	9. Customers seeing their own reminders and charges in the customer portal.
57	10. Month-end agreement between the general ledger and customer accounts.
58	11. Working on both our existing live system and on any new installation.
59	12. Updating the staff guide.
60	
61	### 4.2 Out of scope
62	
63	- Credit insurance and external credit-reference agency feeds.
64	- Debt collection agencies and legal proceedings (we will continue to handle these outside the system, though we want a note of them against the customer).
65	- Changes to how customers pay us, or to cash allocation.
66	- Customer credit applications and account opening.
67	- Supplier (purchase ledger) side.
68	- Changes to price lists, discounts or sales commissions.
69	
70	## 5. Business Requirements
71	
72	### 5.1 Credit reviews
73	
74	- **BR-01** Credit control must be able to record a credit review against any customer. A review records the date, who did it, the outcome (for example: limit confirmed, limit raised, limit reduced, put on watch, put on stop), any new credit limit, free-text notes and the next review date.
75	- **BR-02** Every customer on account must have a next review date. New customers get one automatically when their account is opened, based on a standard review period set by Finance (we expect 12 months, and shorter for higher-risk customers).
76	- **BR-03** The full history of reviews for a customer must be kept and viewable. Past reviews cannot be changed or deleted.
77	- **BR-04** When a review changes the credit limit, the customer's limit must update as part of the review, so the limit and the reason for it are always recorded together.
78	
79	### 5.2 Stop and watch
80	
81	- **BR-05** Credit control must be able to put a customer on stop, with a reason, and take them off stop, with a reason. Each change records who did it and when.
82	- **BR-06** While a customer is on stop, no new orders may be accepted or released for them, by any route: the sales office, the web shop, electronic orders and standing monthly orders. Goods must not be dispatched or invoiced on existing orders taken before the stop, unless credit control releases them.
83	- **BR-07** Only the credit controller and the deputy (and the Finance Director) may put customers on or off stop, or change credit limits. Sales reps and sales office staff must not be able to.
84	- **BR-08** Credit control must be able to put a customer on "watch". A customer on watch can still be supplied, but anyone taking an order for them must be clearly warned, and credit control should be able to see orders taken for watched customers.
85	- **BR-09** A customer's credit status (normal, watch or on stop) must be clearly visible wherever staff look at that customer or take an order for them.
86	- **BR-10** Orders that would take a customer over their credit limit must be held for credit control's approval rather than accepted outright. (Today reps "just put it through".)
87	- **BR-11** Where a customer has asked for or been told about a stop, the customer should see in the web shop that their account is on hold and should contact us, rather than having orders silently fail.
88	
89	### 5.3 Reminder letters (dunning)
90	
91	- **BR-12** The system must send overdue reminder letters in escalating stages. We expect three stages to start with: a polite reminder, a firmer second letter, and a final notice warning that the account will be put on stop and charges applied. Finance must be able to set the number of stages, how many days overdue triggers each stage and the wording of each letter.
92	- **BR-13** Reminders must go by email to the customer's accounts contact. Customers with no email address must be listed so that credit control can post the letter.
93	- **BR-14** Reminders are produced in a regular run (we expect weekly) started by credit control. Before sending, credit control must be able to see who will get which letter and leave out particular customers (for example, where a payment has been promised or there is a dispute).
94	- **BR-15** A customer should only move up a stage if they are still overdue; a customer who pays must not get the next letter. A customer must not receive the same stage twice in a short time.
95	- **BR-16** Every reminder sent must be recorded against the customer: the date, the stage, what invoices it covered and the amount.
96	- **BR-17** Reminders must be in the customer's own currency and show their overdue invoices.
97	- **BR-18** Credit control should be able to mark an invoice as disputed, so that it is not chased and not charged interest until the dispute is settled.
98	
99	### 5.4 Interest and late fees
100	
101	- **BR-19** At month end the system must be able to charge interest on overdue balances, a fixed late fee, or both. Finance must be able to set the interest rate, the fee amount and how many days overdue a balance must be before it is charged.
102	- **BR-20** It must be possible to exempt individual customers from interest and/or fees (for example, key accounts or those with agreed payment plans).
103	- **BR-21** Charges must be raised in the customer's own currency and must appear on the customer's account and their next statement as separate, clearly described items.
104	- **BR-22** Before charges are posted, credit control must be able to see a list of what will be charged to whom, and confirm it. The same month must not be charged twice.
105	- **BR-23** Interest and fees must post to the general ledger to the income accounts that Finance chooses.
106	- **BR-24** Credit control must be able to waive (reverse) a charge for a customer, with a reason, and the reversal must also reach the ledger.
107	
108	### 5.5 Bad debt write-off
109	
110	- **BR-25** Credit control must be able to write off all or part of a customer's unpaid balance as a bad debt, with a reason.
111	- **BR-26** Write-offs above an amount set by Finance must be approved by the Finance Director before they take effect.
112	- **BR-27** A write-off must reduce the customer's balance and post to the bad debt account in the general ledger, including any currency difference.
113	- **BR-28** When a customer has a debt written off, the customer should be put on stop automatically, unless credit control decides otherwise.
114	- **BR-29** There must be a report of write-offs over a period, showing customer, amount, reason, who did it and who approved it.
115	
116	### 5.6 Reporting
117	
118	- **BR-30** A credit control report must list customers who are due or overdue for a credit review, customers over their credit limit (and by how much), and customers on watch or on stop. It must be filterable by sales rep and by currency, and totals must be shown in our home currency.
119	- **BR-31** The aged debt report must show each customer's credit status, credit limit and the last reminder stage sent.
120	- **BR-32** All credit control actions (reviews, stop/watch changes, limit changes, reminders, charges, waivers and write-offs) must be visible as a history per customer that the auditors can inspect.
121	
122	### 5.7 Sales reps
123	
124	- **BR-33** Sales reps must see credit information (status, limit, balance, overdue amounts, reminders) only for their own customers, not for other reps' customers.
125	- **BR-34** Reps can see but not change credit status or limits.
126	
127	### 5.8 Customer portal
128	
129	- **BR-35** Customers who log in to the portal must be able to see the reminder letters we have sent them and the interest and fees charged to their account, along with their balance.
130	- **BR-36** A customer must only ever see their own account.
131	
132	### 5.9 Month end and the ledger
133	
134	- **BR-37** At month end the total of all customer balances must agree with the trade debtors control account in the general ledger, after interest, fees, waivers and write-offs have been posted.
135	- **BR-38** If they do not agree, Finance must be able to find out why from the system.
136	
137	### 5.10 Installation and rollout
138	
139	- **BR-39** The capability must work on our existing live system, with all our existing customers, balances and history, as well as on a brand-new installation.
140	- **BR-40** On go-live every existing customer starts as "normal", with a next review date set by Finance, unless credit control loads their current status from the spreadsheet. Existing customers who are on the spreadsheet stop list today must be on stop in the system from day one.
141	- **BR-41** Nothing in the new capability should change how existing invoices, statements or postings behave for customers who are not overdue.
142	
143	### 5.11 Documentation and training
144	
145	- **BR-42** The staff guide must be updated to explain credit reviews, stop and watch, the reminder run, month-end charges, write-offs and the credit control report.
146	- **BR-43** Sales staff need a short note on what "watch" and "stop" mean for them and who to contact.
147	
148	## 6. User Stories
149	
150	1. **As Maria (credit controller)**, I want to see every Monday which customers are due a review or over their limit, so that I can work through them in order and nothing slips.
151	2. **As Maria**, I want to put a customer on stop once, and know that the sales office, the web shop, EDI orders and the standing orders are all blocked, so that I don't have to phone round.
152	3. **As the deputy credit controller**, I want the same powers and the same history as Maria, so that I can cover her holidays without asking her what she agreed with whom.
153	4. **As a sales rep**, I want to see when one of my customers is on watch or on stop, and why, so that I can talk to the customer before they place an order.
154	5. **As Maria**, I want the weekly reminder run to email the right letter at the right stage to each overdue customer, after I've had a chance to take out the ones I'm already talking to.
155	6. **As the Financial Accountant**, I want month-end interest and fees to post themselves to the ledger, so that the debtors control account agrees with the customer balances without manual journals.
156	7. **As the Finance Director**, I want to approve large write-offs before they go through, so that I know what bad debt we are taking.
157	8. **As a customer**, I want to see in the portal the reminders and charges on my account, so that I understand what I owe and why.
158	9. **As the external auditor**, I want to see for any customer who changed their credit limit or status, when and why, so that I can test the credit control process.
159	
160	## 7. Acceptance Criteria (business terms)
161	
162	- **AC-01** Maria records a review on a customer, raising their limit and setting next review in six months. The new limit applies straight away, and the review, with her notes, appears in the customer's history. The customer drops off the "due for review" list and reappears when the next date comes round.
163	- **AC-02** A customer is put on stop. An order for them cannot be completed in the sales office, through the web shop, electronically or from their standing order. When they are taken off stop, orders go through again. Both changes appear in their history with reasons.
164	- **AC-03** A sales rep tries to take a customer off stop or raise a limit and cannot.
165	- **AC-04** A customer on watch places an order: it is accepted, the person taking it sees a warning, and the order shows on credit control's list.
166	- **AC-05** An order that would take a customer over their limit is held and only released when credit control approves it.
167	- **AC-06** In the reminder run, a customer 35 days overdue gets the first letter by email; the next run, if still unpaid and past the second threshold, they get the second letter; if they pay in between, they get nothing. A customer marked disputed gets no letter. Every letter sent shows on the customer's account history and in their portal.
168	- **AC-07** At month end, an overdue customer is charged interest at the set rate and the set late fee in their own currency; an exempt customer is not charged; running the charges again for the same month charges nobody twice. The charges appear on the customer's statement and in the portal.
169	- **AC-08** After month-end charges, waivers and write-offs, the total of customer balances equals the debtors control account in the general ledger.
170	- **AC-09** A write-off below the approval amount reduces the customer's balance and appears in the bad debt account; one above it does nothing until the Finance Director approves it. The customer is put on stop.
171	- **AC-10** Rep A sees credit details for her customers and none for Rep B's customers. Customer X in the portal sees only Customer X's reminders and charges.
172	- **AC-11** After go-live on the live system, all existing customers, balances and history are intact, every customer has a next review date, and everyone on the old spreadsheet stop list is on stop.
173	- **AC-12** The updated staff guide covers every item in section 4.1 and has been read and agreed by Maria and the Sales Manager.
174	
175	## 8. Assumptions
176	
177	- Customers' accounts contact email addresses are mostly up to date; credit control will clean up the rest before go-live.
178	- Each customer already has a single sales rep assigned.
179	- Our terms and conditions allow us to charge interest and late fees; Legal will confirm the wording for letters.
180	- Credit control will provide the current stop list and credit limits from the spreadsheet for go-live.
181	
182	## 9. Open Questions
183	
184	1. Interest: a simple annual rate on overdue balances, or a statutory late-payment rate? Does it differ by currency or country?
185	2. Late fee: one flat fee per month, or a fee per overdue invoice? Should it vary by currency?
186	3. Do we charge interest on interest and fees that are themselves overdue?
187	4. Should a customer be put on stop automatically after the final reminder, or only flagged for Maria to decide?
188	5. How should over-limit orders from the web shop and standing orders be handled: held for approval, or rejected with a message to the customer?
189	6. What is the approval threshold for write-offs, and does the Financial Accountant also need to sign off?
190	7. If a written-off debt is later paid, how do we want it shown?
191	8. Should reps be told the reason for a stop, or only that the customer is on stop?
192	9. Do we need the reminder letters in languages other than English for overseas customers?
193	10. Should customers be able to see "watch" status in the portal? (Our view: no.)
194	11. Who covers credit decisions when both Maria and her deputy are away?
195	12. Do head-office/branch customer groups share one credit limit, or does each branch have its own?

9. **As the external auditor**, I want to see for any customer who changed their credit limit or status, when and why, so that I can test the credit control process.

## 7. Acceptance Criteria (business terms)

- **AC-01** Maria records a review on a customer, raising their limit and setting next review in six months. The new limit applies straight away, and the review, with her notes, appears in the customer's history. The customer drops off the "due for review" list and reappears when the next date comes round.
- **AC-02** A customer is put on stop. An order for them cannot be completed in the sales office, through the web shop, electronically or from their standing order. When they are taken off stop, orders go through again. Both changes appear in their history with reasons.
- **AC-03** A sales rep tries to take a customer off stop or raise a limit and cannot.
- **AC-04** A customer on watch places an order: it is accepted, the person taking it sees a warning, and the order shows on credit control's list.
- **AC-05** An order that would take a customer over their limit is held and only released when credit control approves it.
- **AC-06** In the reminder run, a customer 35 days overdue gets the first letter by email; the next run, if still unpaid and past the second threshold, they get the second letter; if they pay in between, they get nothing. A customer marked disputed gets no letter. Every letter sent shows on the customer's account history and in their portal.
- **AC-07** At month end, an overdue customer is charged interest at the set rate and the set late fee in their own currency; an exempt customer is not charged; running the charges again for the same month charges nobody twice. The charges appear on the customer's statement and in the portal.
- **AC-08** After month-end charges, waivers and write-offs, the total of customer balances equals the debtors control account in the general ledger.
- **AC-09** A write-off below the approval amount reduces the customer's balance and appears in the bad debt account; one above it does nothing until the Finance Director approves it. The customer is put on stop.
- **AC-10** Rep A sees credit details for her customers and none for Rep B's customers. Customer X in the portal sees only Customer X's reminders and charges.
- **AC-11** After go-live on the live system, all existing customers, balances and history are intact, every customer has a next review date, and everyone on the old spreadsheet stop list is on stop.
- **AC-12** The updated staff guide covers every item in section 4.1 and has been read and agreed by Maria and the Sales Manager.

## 8. Assumptions

- Customers' accounts contact email addresses are mostly up to date; credit control will clean up the rest before go-live.
- Each customer already has a single sales rep assigned.
- Our terms and conditions allow us to charge interest and late fees; Legal will confirm the wording for letters.
- Credit control will provide the current stop list and credit limits from the spreadsheet for go-live.

## 9. Open Questions

1. Interest: a simple annual rate on overdue balances, or a statutory late-payment rate? Does it differ by currency or country?
2. Late fee: one flat fee per month, or a fee per overdue invoice? Should it vary by currency?
3. Do we charge interest on interest and fees that are themselves overdue?
4. Should a customer be put on stop automatically after the final reminder, or only flagged for Maria to decide?
5. How should over-limit orders from the web shop and standing orders be handled: held for approval, or rejected with a message to the customer?
6. What is the approval threshold for write-offs, and does the Financial Accountant also need to sign off?
7. If a written-off debt is later paid, how do we want it shown?
8. Should reps be told the reason for a stop, or only that the customer is on stop?
9. Do we need the reminder letters in languages other than English for overseas customers?
10. Should customers be able to see "watch" status in the portal? (Our view: no.)
11. Who covers credit decisions when both Maria and her deputy are away?
12. Do head-office/branch customer groups share one credit limit, or does each branch have its own?

//
//     SELECT 
//         TABLE_NAME AS 'Referencing Table', 
//         COLUMN_NAME AS 'Foreign Key Column',

//   +-----------------------------+--------------------+------------------------------------+
//   | bom                         | parent             | bom_ibfk_1                         |
//   | bom                         | component          | bom_ibfk_2                         |

<?php

/* Credit control: reviews, stop/watch, dunning, interest and fees, write-offs.
 *
 * Stop and watch are NOT new concepts - webERP already carries them on debtorsmaster.holdreason, where the
 * holdreasons.dissallowinvoices flag is 0 = normal, 1 = stop (no orders or invoices), 2 = watch.
 * This update adds what was missing around that: history, reminders, charges, write-offs and the per-customer fields.
 */

// Customer fields
AddColumn('nextreviewdate', 'debtorsmaster', 'date', 'NULL', '', 'language_id');
AddColumn('chargeexempt', 'debtorsmaster', 'tinyint', 'NOT NULL', '0', 'nextreviewdate');
AddIndex(array('nextreviewdate'), 'debtorsmaster', 'nextreviewdate');

// A disputed invoice is neither chased nor charged interest
AddColumn('disputed', 'debtortrans', 'tinyint', 'NOT NULL', '0', 'salesperson');

// 0 = not held, 1 = held for credit control, 2 = released by credit control
AddColumn('creditholdstate', 'salesorders', 'tinyint', 'NOT NULL', '0', 'internalcomment');

CreateTable('creditreviews',
"CREATE TABLE `creditreviews` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `reviewdate` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01 00:00:00',
  `userid` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `outcome` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `oldlimit` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `newlimit` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `notes` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `nextreviewdate` date DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`),
  KEY `reviewdate` (`reviewdate`),
  CONSTRAINT `creditreviews_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`debtorno`) REFERENCES `debtorsmaster` (`debtorno`)
)");

CreateTable('creditevents',
"CREATE TABLE `creditevents` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `eventdate` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01 00:00:00',
  `userid` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `eventtype` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `reason` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `amount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `currcode` char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `reference` varchar(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`),
  KEY `eventdate` (`eventdate`),
  KEY `eventtype` (`eventtype`),
  CONSTRAINT `creditevents_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`debtorno`) REFERENCES `debtorsmaster` (`debtorno`)
)");

CreateTable('dunningstages',
"CREATE TABLE `dunningstages` (
  `stage` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  `daysoverdue` smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT '30',
  `subject` varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `body` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`stage`)
)");

CreateTable('dunninglog',
"CREATE TABLE `dunninglog` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `stage` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  `sentdate` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01 00:00:00',
  `userid` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `currcode` char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `amount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `invoices` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `method` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'email',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`,`stage`),
  KEY `sentdate` (`sentdate`),
  CONSTRAINT `dunninglog_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`debtorno`) REFERENCES `debtorsmaster` (`debtorno`)
)");

CreateTable('creditcharges',
"CREATE TABLE `creditcharges` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `chargemonth` char(7) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `chargetype` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'interest',
  `currcode` char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `amount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `transno` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `posteddate` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01 00:00:00',
  `postedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `waived` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `waivedtransno` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `waiveddate` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `waivedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `waivereason` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `onechargepermonth` (`debtorno`,`chargemonth`,`chargetype`),
  KEY `chargemonth` (`chargemonth`),
  CONSTRAINT `creditcharges_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`debtorno`) REFERENCES `debtorsmaster` (`debtorno`)
)");

CreateTable('creditwriteoffs',
"CREATE TABLE `creditwriteoffs` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `requestdate` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01 00:00:00',
  `requestedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `currcode` char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `amount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `homeamount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `reason` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `status` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  `approvedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `approvaldate` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `posteddate` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `transno` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `putonstop` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`),
  KEY `status` (`status`),
  CONSTRAINT `creditwriteoffs_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`debtorno`) REFERENCES `debtorsmaster` (`debtorno`)
)");

// New transaction types, so that charges, waivers and write-offs are distinguishable on the customer account,
// on statements and in the GL, and so that they keep their own number sequence
NewSysType(51, 'Customer Interest and Fees');
NewSysType(52, 'Customer Charge Waiver');
NewSysType(53, 'Bad Debt Write-off');

// Security: 21 = credit control staff (stop, limits, reviews, reminders, charges, write-off requests),
// 22 = credit control authority (Finance Director: approve large write-offs, change credit control settings).
// Assign them to the right roles in Access Permissions - by default the Accountant and System Administrator roles get them.
NewSecurityToken(21, 'Credit Control');
NewSecurityToken(22, 'Credit Control Authority - approve write-offs and change settings');
InsertRecord('securitygroups', array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(6, 21), array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(6, 21));
InsertRecord('securitygroups', array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(8, 21), array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(8, 21));
InsertRecord('securitygroups', array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(8, 22), array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(8, 22));

NewScript('CreditControl.php', 1);
NewScript('CreditCustomer.php', 1);
NewScript('CreditReminders.php', 21);
NewScript('CreditCharges.php', 21);
NewScript('CreditWriteOffs.php', 21);
NewScript('CreditControlSettings.php', 22);
NewScript('CustomerCreditPortal.php', 1);

NewMenuItem('AR', 'Transactions', __('Credit Control Worklist'), '/CreditControl.php', 5);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Transactions', __('Credit Reminder Run'), '/CreditReminders.php', 6);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Transactions', __('Month End Interest and Fees'), '/CreditCharges.php', 7);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Transactions', __('Bad Debt Write-offs'), '/CreditWriteOffs.php', 8);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Maintenance', __('Credit Control Settings'), '/CreditControlSettings.php', 3);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Reports', __('My Account - Reminders and Charges'), '/CustomerCreditPortal.php', 11);

// Settings. GL accounts are deliberately left blank: Finance must choose them before charges or write-offs can be posted.
NewConfigValue('CreditReviewMonths', '12');
NewConfigValue('CreditInterestRate', '0');
NewConfigValue('CreditLateFee', '0');
NewConfigValue('CreditChargeDays', '30');
NewConfigValue('CreditFeePerInvoice', '0');
NewConfigValue('CreditInterestOnCharges', '0');
NewConfigValue('CreditInterestAct', '');
NewConfigValue('CreditLateFeeAct', '');
NewConfigValue('CreditBadDebtAct', '');
NewConfigValue('CreditWriteOffLimit', '1000');
NewConfigValue('CreditStopOnWriteOff', '1');
NewConfigValue('CreditDunningMinDays', '14');

// Which hold reasons credit control uses for normal / watch / stop. Reuse what the customer already has defined,
// and create a reason only where none of that kind exists.
$HoldKinds = array('CreditNormalHoldReason' => array(0, __('Credit control - normal')),
					'CreditWatchHoldReason' => array(2, __('Credit control - watch')),
					'CreditStopHoldReason' => array(1, __('Credit control - stop')));
foreach ($HoldKinds as $ConfName => $Kind) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT reasoncode FROM holdreasons WHERE dissallowinvoices = " . $Kind[0] . " ORDER BY reasoncode LIMIT 1");
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		$Result = DB_query("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(reasoncode), 0) + 1 FROM holdreasons");
		$Row = DB_fetch_row($Result);
		InsertRecord('holdreasons', array('reasoncode'), array($Row[0]), array('reasoncode', 'reasondescription', 'dissallowinvoices'), array($Row[0], $Kind[1], $Kind[0]));
		$Code = $Row[0];
	} else {
		$Row = DB_fetch_row($Result);
		$Code = $Row[0];
	}
	NewConfigValue($ConfName, $Code);
}

// Three escalating letters to start with. Finance edits the wording and the day thresholds in Credit Control Settings.
// The placeholders are replaced when the letter is produced.
InsertRecord('dunningstages', array('stage'), array(1), array('stage', 'daysoverdue', 'subject', 'body'),
	array(1, 30, 'Reminder: overdue account', "Dear [CUSTOMER],\n\nOur records show that the invoices listed below are past their due date. The total overdue is [CURRENCY] [AMOUNT].\n\n[INVOICES]\n\nIf you have already paid, please disregard this letter. Otherwise please arrange payment as soon as possible.\n\nKind regards\n[COMPANY]"));
InsertRecord('dunningstages', array('stage'), array(2), array('stage', 'daysoverdue', 'subject', 'body'),
	array(2, 45, 'Second reminder: overdue account', "Dear [CUSTOMER],\n\nWe wrote to you recently about overdue invoices and have not yet received payment. The total overdue is [CURRENCY] [AMOUNT].\n\n[INVOICES]\n\nPlease pay immediately or contact us today if there is a problem with any of these invoices.\n\nKind regards\n[COMPANY]"));
InsertRecord('dunningstages', array('stage'), array(3), array('stage', 'daysoverdue', 'subject', 'body'),
	array(3, 60, 'FINAL NOTICE: overdue account', "Dear [CUSTOMER],\n\nThis is a final notice. The total overdue on your account is [CURRENCY] [AMOUNT].\n\n[INVOICES]\n\nIf we do not receive payment within 7 days your account will be put on stop, no further orders will be accepted and late payment charges will be applied.\n\nKind regards\n[COMPANY]"));

// Every existing customer starts as normal (their current hold reason is kept - customers already on stop stay on stop)
// with a next review date one standard review period from now. Credit control can then reschedule from the worklist.
executeSQL("UPDATE debtorsmaster SET nextreviewdate = DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 12 MONTH) WHERE nextreviewdate IS NULL", false);

// Existing hold-reason based stops are legitimate, but they have no history; record the starting position once.
executeSQL("INSERT INTO creditevents (debtorno, eventdate, userid, eventtype, reason, currcode)
			SELECT debtorsmaster.debtorno, NOW(), 'system',
					CASE holdreasons.dissallowinvoices WHEN 1 THEN 'stop' ELSE 'watch' END,
					CONCAT('Status at go-live: ', holdreasons.reasondescription),
					debtorsmaster.currcode
			FROM debtorsmaster INNER JOIN holdreasons ON debtorsmaster.holdreason = holdreasons.reasoncode
			WHERE holdreasons.dissallowinvoices IN (1, 2)
			AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM creditevents WHERE creditevents.debtorno = debtorsmaster.debtorno)", false);

if ($_SESSION['Updates']['Errors'] == 0) {
	UpdateDBNo(basename(__FILE__, '.php'), __('Credit control: reviews, reminders, interest and fees, write-offs'));
}

 * This update adds what was missing around that: history, reminders, charges, write-offs and the per-customer fields.
 */

// Customer fields
AddColumn('nextreviewdate', 'debtorsmaster', 'date', 'NULL', '', 'language_id');
AddColumn('chargeexempt', 'debtorsmaster', 'tinyint', 'NOT NULL', '0', 'nextreviewdate');
AddIndex(array('nextreviewdate'), 'debtorsmaster', 'nextreviewdate');

// A disputed invoice is neither chased nor charged interest
AddColumn('disputed', 'debtortrans', 'tinyint', 'NOT NULL', '0', 'salesperson');

// 0 = not held, 1 = held for credit control, 2 = released by credit control
AddColumn('creditholdstate', 'salesorders', 'tinyint', 'NOT NULL', '0', 'internalcomment');

CreateTable('creditreviews',
"CREATE TABLE `creditreviews` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `reviewdate` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01 00:00:00',
  `userid` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `outcome` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `oldlimit` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `newlimit` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `notes` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `nextreviewdate` date DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`),
  KEY `reviewdate` (`reviewdate`),
  CONSTRAINT `creditreviews_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`debtorno`) REFERENCES `debtorsmaster` (`debtorno`)
)");

CreateTable('creditevents',
"CREATE TABLE `creditevents` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `eventdate` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01 00:00:00',
  `userid` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',

  `reason` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `amount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `currcode` char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `reference` varchar(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`),
  KEY `eventdate` (`eventdate`),
  KEY `eventtype` (`eventtype`),
  CONSTRAINT `creditevents_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`debtorno`) REFERENCES `debtorsmaster` (`debtorno`)
)");

CreateTable('dunningstages',
"CREATE TABLE `dunningstages` (
  `stage` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',

  `subject` varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `body` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`stage`)
)");

"CREATE TABLE `dunninglog` (

  `sentdate` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01 00:00:00',

input.content:
<?php

/* Shared credit control logic.
 *
 * Credit status is NOT a new field: it is the existing debtorsmaster.holdreason, whose holdreasons.dissallowinvoices
 * flag has always meant 0 = normal, 1 = stop (no orders, no invoices), 2 = watch. Everything that already checks that
 * flag (order entry, counter sales, statements, customer inquiry...) therefore keeps working; credit control adds the
 * history, the controlled way of changing it and the missing enforcement points.
 *
 * All $_POST / $_GET values are already escaped by session.php; values read from the database are escaped here
 * with DB_escape_string() only where they are written back.
 */

define('CREDIT_NORMAL', 0);
define('CREDIT_STOP', 1);
define('CREDIT_WATCH', 2);

/* Systypes for the transactions created by credit control */
define('CREDIT_TYPE_CHARGE', 51);
define('CREDIT_TYPE_WAIVER', 52);
define('CREDIT_TYPE_WRITEOFF', 53);

function CreditUserHasToken($Token) {
	return isset($_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']) and in_array($Token, $_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']);
}

/* Credit control staff: may stop/release customers, change limits, review, remind, charge, request write-offs */
function CreditUserCanManage() {
	return CreditUserHasToken(21);
}

/* Credit control authority (Finance Director): approve write-offs, change settings */
function CreditUserCanApprove() {
	return CreditUserHasToken(22);
}

function CreditStatusLabel($DisallowFlag) {
	if ($DisallowFlag == CREDIT_STOP) {
		return __('On Stop');
	} elseif ($DisallowFlag == CREDIT_WATCH) {
		return __('Watch');
	}
	return __('Normal');
}

function CreditStatusCssClass($DisallowFlag) {
	if ($DisallowFlag == CREDIT_STOP) {
		return 'error';
	} elseif ($DisallowFlag == CREDIT_WATCH) {
		return 'warn';
	}
	return 'success';
}

/* Sales reps (users with a salesman code) only ever see their own customers */
function CreditRepFilterSQL($DebtorField = 'debtorsmaster.debtorno') {
	if (isset($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) and $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] != '') {
		return " AND " . $DebtorField . " IN (SELECT debtorno FROM custbranch WHERE salesman = '" . $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] . "') ";
	}
	return '';
}

function CreditRepCanSee($DebtorNo) {
	if (!isset($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) or $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] == '') {
		return true;
	}
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM custbranch WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "' AND salesman = '" . $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] . "'");
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return $MyRow[0] > 0;
}

/* The debtor number of a customer-portal user, read fresh from the database so it cannot be changed through the session
 * or the URL. Returns '' for staff users. */
function CreditPortalCustomer() {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT customerid FROM www_users WHERE userid = '" . $_SESSION['UserID'] . "'");
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return $MyRow ? $MyRow[0] : '';
}

/* The hold reason code credit control uses for 'normal', 'watch' or 'stop'.
 * Uses the configured code if it still exists with the right kind of flag, otherwise the lowest code of that kind.
 * Returns null if no hold reason of that kind exists (the caller must tell the user to define one in Credit Status). */
function CreditHoldReasonCode($Kind) {
	$Map = array('normal' => array('CreditNormalHoldReason', CREDIT_NORMAL),
				'watch' => array('CreditWatchHoldReason', CREDIT_WATCH),
				'stop' => array('CreditStopHoldReason', CREDIT_STOP));
	$ConfName = $Map[$Kind][0];
	$Flag = $Map[$Kind][1];
	if (isset($_SESSION[$ConfName]) and $_SESSION[$ConfName] !== '') {
		$Result = DB_query("SELECT reasoncode FROM holdreasons WHERE reasoncode = '" . $_SESSION[$ConfName] . "' AND dissallowinvoices = " . $Flag);
		if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 1) {
			return $_SESSION[$ConfName];
		}
	}
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT reasoncode FROM holdreasons WHERE dissallowinvoices = " . $Flag . " ORDER BY reasoncode LIMIT 1");
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 1) {
		$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
		return $MyRow[0];
	}
	return null;
}

/* Customer credit header: name, currency, limit, status flag and description, review date, exemption, balance.
 * Returns false if the customer does not exist. */
function CreditCustomerRecord($DebtorNo) {
	$SQL = "SELECT debtorsmaster.debtorno,
					debtorsmaster.name,
					debtorsmaster.currcode,
					debtorsmaster.creditlimit,
					debtorsmaster.holdreason,
					debtorsmaster.nextreviewdate,
					debtorsmaster.chargeexempt,
					holdreasons.dissallowinvoices,
					holdreasons.reasondescription,
					currencies.decimalplaces,
					currencies.rate
			FROM debtorsmaster
			INNER JOIN holdreasons ON debtorsmaster.holdreason = holdreasons.reasoncode
			INNER JOIN currencies ON debtorsmaster.currcode = currencies.currabrev
			WHERE debtorsmaster.debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return false;
	}
	$Record = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(balance), 0) FROM debtortrans WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'");
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	$Record['balance'] = $MyRow[0];
	return $Record;
}

function LogCreditEvent($DebtorNo, $EventType, $Reason = '', $Amount = 0, $CurrCode = '', $Reference = '') {
	$SQL = "INSERT INTO creditevents (debtorno, eventdate, userid, eventtype, reason, amount, currcode, reference)
			VALUES ('" . $DebtorNo . "',
					NOW(),
					'" . (isset($_SESSION['UserID']) ? $_SESSION['UserID'] : 'system') . "',
					'" . $EventType . "',
					'" . DB_escape_string($Reason) . "',
					'" . $Amount . "',
					'" . $CurrCode . "',
					'" . $Reference . "')";
	DB_query($SQL, __('The credit control history could not be recorded because'));
}

/* Move a customer to 'normal', 'watch' or 'stop' and record who did it and why.
 * Returns '' on success or an error message. The caller is responsible for the transaction. */
function CreditSetStatus($DebtorNo, $Kind, $Reason) {
	$Customer = CreditCustomerRecord($DebtorNo);
	if ($Customer === false) {
		return __('The customer does not exist');
	}
	$NewCode = CreditHoldReasonCode($Kind);
	if ($NewCode === null) {
		return __('No credit status of this kind is defined. Define one in Credit Status Maintenance first');
	}
	$OldFlag = $Customer['dissallowinvoices'];
	$NewFlag = ($Kind == 'stop' ? CREDIT_STOP : ($Kind == 'watch' ? CREDIT_WATCH : CREDIT_NORMAL));
	if ($OldFlag == $NewFlag and $Customer['holdreason'] == $NewCode) {
		return '';
	}
	DB_query("UPDATE debtorsmaster SET holdreason = '" . $NewCode . "' WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'",
			__('The credit status could not be updated because'));
	if ($NewFlag == CREDIT_STOP) {
		$EventType = 'stop';
	} elseif ($OldFlag == CREDIT_STOP) {
		$EventType = 'unstop';
	} elseif ($NewFlag == CREDIT_WATCH) {
		$EventType = 'watch';
	} else {
		$EventType = 'unwatch';
	}
	LogCreditEvent($DebtorNo, $EventType, $Reason, 0, $Customer['currcode']);
	return '';
}

/* Change the credit limit and record the change with its reason. The caller is responsible for the transaction. */
function CreditSetLimit($DebtorNo, $NewLimit, $Reason) {
	$Customer = CreditCustomerRecord($DebtorNo);
	if ($Customer === false or abs($Customer['creditlimit'] - $NewLimit) < 0.005) {
		return;
	}
	DB_query("UPDATE debtorsmaster SET creditlimit = '" . $NewLimit . "' WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'",
			__('The credit limit could not be updated because'));
	LogCreditEvent($DebtorNo, 'limit', $Reason . ' (' . locale_number_format($Customer['creditlimit'], 0) . ' -> ' . locale_number_format($NewLimit, 0) . ')', $NewLimit, $Customer['currcode']);
}

/* The next review date for a customer reviewed today */
function CreditNextReviewDate($FromDate = '') {
	$Months = isset($_SESSION['CreditReviewMonths']) ? (int)$_SESSION['CreditReviewMonths'] : 12;
	if ($Months < 1) {
		$Months = 12;
	}
	$From = ($FromDate == '' ? time() : strtotime($FromDate));
	return date('Y-m-d', strtotime('+' . $Months . ' months', $From));
}

/* Value of the lines of an order cart in the customer's currency, including freight. */
function CreditCartValue($Cart) {
	$Value = 0;
	foreach ($Cart->LineItems as $LineItem) {
		$Value += $LineItem->Price * $LineItem->Quantity * (1 - $LineItem->DiscountPercent);
	}
	return $Value + $Cart->FreightCost;
}

/* What may happen to a new order for this customer?
 *   stop      - the customer is on stop: the order must be refused
 *   watch     - the customer is on watch: accept, but warn
 *   hold      - CheckCreditLimits is 3 and the order would take the customer over their limit: accept, but hold it
 *               for credit control approval
 *   overlimit - the order would take the customer over their limit (whatever the CheckCreditLimits setting)
 * $OrderValue is the value of the order about to be created, in the customer's currency. */
function CreditOrderCheck($DebtorNo, $OrderValue = 0) {
	$Check = array('stop' => false, 'watch' => false, 'hold' => false, 'overlimit' => false, 'available' => 0);
	$Customer = CreditCustomerRecord($DebtorNo);
	if ($Customer === false) {
		return $Check;
	}
	$Check['stop'] = ($Customer['dissallowinvoices'] == CREDIT_STOP);
	$Check['watch'] = ($Customer['dissallowinvoices'] == CREDIT_WATCH);
	if (!function_exists('GetCreditAvailable')) {
		include_once(__DIR__ . '/SQL_CommonFunctions.php');
	}
	$Check['available'] = GetCreditAvailable($DebtorNo) - $OrderValue;
	$Check['overlimit'] = ($Check['available'] < 0);
	$Check['hold'] = ($Check['overlimit'] and isset($_SESSION['CheckCreditLimits']) and $_SESSION['CheckCreditLimits'] == 3);
	return $Check;
}

/* May goods be dispatched / an order be invoiced?  Returns '' if yes, otherwise the reason it may not.
 * An order is released for invoicing when credit control has explicitly released it (creditholdstate = 2),
 * or when the customer is not on stop and the order is not held for approval. */
function CreditOrderBlockReason($OrderNo) {
	$SQL = "SELECT salesorders.creditholdstate,
					holdreasons.dissallowinvoices
			FROM salesorders
			INNER JOIN debtorsmaster ON salesorders.debtorno = debtorsmaster.debtorno
			INNER JOIN holdreasons ON debtorsmaster.holdreason = holdreasons.reasoncode
			WHERE salesorders.orderno = '" . (int)$OrderNo . "'";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return '';
	}
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	if ($MyRow['creditholdstate'] == 2) {
		return '';
	}
	if ($MyRow['creditholdstate'] == 1) {
		return __('This order is held for credit control approval and cannot be dispatched or invoiced until it is released');
	}
	if ($MyRow['dissallowinvoices'] == CREDIT_STOP) {
		return __('This customer is on stop. The order cannot be dispatched or invoiced until credit control takes the customer off stop or releases the order');
	}
	return '';
}

/* SQL expression for the due date of a debtor transaction (needs debtortrans and paymentterms in the query) */
function CreditDueDateSQL() {
	return "CASE WHEN paymentterms.daysbeforedue > 0
				THEN DATE_ADD(debtortrans.trandate, INTERVAL paymentterms.daysbeforedue DAY)
				ELSE DATE_ADD(LAST_DAY(debtortrans.trandate), INTERVAL paymentterms.dayinfollowingmonth DAY)
			END";
}

/* Open positive items of a customer that are past their due date as at $AsAt (Y-m-d), oldest first.
 * Disputed items are excluded. Interest and fee charges are included only when $IncludeCharges is true, because they are
 * chased but - unless Finance decides otherwise - do not themselves attract interest. */
function CreditOverdueItems($DebtorNo, $AsAt, $MinDaysOverdue = 1, $IncludeCharges = true) {
	$DueSQL = CreditDueDateSQL();
	$SQL = "SELECT debtortrans.id,
					debtortrans.type,
					debtortrans.transno,
					debtortrans.trandate,
					debtortrans.reference,
					debtortrans.balance,
					debtortrans.rate,
					" . $DueSQL . " AS duedate,
					DATEDIFF('" . $AsAt . "', " . $DueSQL . ") AS daysoverdue
			FROM debtortrans
			INNER JOIN debtorsmaster ON debtortrans.debtorno = debtorsmaster.debtorno
			INNER JOIN paymentterms ON debtorsmaster.paymentterms = paymentterms.termsindicator
			WHERE debtortrans.debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'
				AND debtortrans.balance > 0.005
				AND debtortrans.disputed = 0
				AND debtortrans.trandate <= '" . $AsAt . "'
				AND DATEDIFF('" . $AsAt . "', " . $DueSQL . ") >= " . (int)$MinDaysOverdue .
				($IncludeCharges ? "" : " AND debtortrans.type <> " . CREDIT_TYPE_CHARGE) . "
			ORDER BY debtortrans.trandate, debtortrans.transno";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	$Items = array();
	while ($MyRow = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
		$Items[] = $MyRow;
	}
	return $Items;
}

/* Unallocated credit (receipts, credit notes) of a customer: it reduces what is really overdue, so a customer who has paid
 * but whose cash has not yet been allocated is not chased or charged. Returned as a positive number. */
function CreditUnallocatedCredit($DebtorNo) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(-balance), 0) FROM debtortrans WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "' AND balance < -0.005");
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return $MyRow[0];
}

/* The overdue position of a customer: net amount overdue after unallocated credits, oldest overdue item, days overdue */
function CreditOverduePosition($DebtorNo, $AsAt, $MinDaysOverdue = 1, $IncludeCharges = true) {
	$Items = CreditOverdueItems($DebtorNo, $AsAt, $MinDaysOverdue, $IncludeCharges);
	$Gross = 0;
	$MaxDays = 0;
	foreach ($Items as $Item) {
		$Gross += $Item['balance'];
		$MaxDays = max($MaxDays, $Item['daysoverdue']);
	}
	$Net = max(0, $Gross - CreditUnallocatedCredit($DebtorNo));
	return array('items' => $Items, 'gross' => $Gross, 'net' => $Net, 'maxdays' => $MaxDays);
}

/* Reminder stages, lowest first: array of rows (stage, daysoverdue, subject, body) */
function CreditDunningStages() {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT stage, daysoverdue, subject, body FROM dunningstages ORDER BY daysoverdue, stage");
	$Stages = array();
	while ($MyRow = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
		$Stages[] = $MyRow;
	}
	return $Stages;
}

/* The highest reminder stage ever sent to the customer, 0 if none (used by the aged debtors report) */
function CreditLastReminderStage($DebtorNo) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(stage), 0) FROM dunninglog WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'");
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return $MyRow[0];
}

/* Which reminder (if any) is due for this customer today?
 * Returns array('stage' => row or null, 'reason' => why nothing is due, 'position' => overdue position).
 * A customer only moves up a stage while still overdue (net of unallocated credits), never receives a stage already sent for
 * the current run of overdue invoices, and never receives two letters within CreditDunningMinDays. */
function CreditReminderDue($DebtorNo, $AsAt, $Stages) {
	$Position = CreditOverduePosition($DebtorNo, $AsAt);
	$Due = array('stage' => null, 'reason' => '', 'position' => $Position);
	if ($Position['net'] <= 0.005 or count($Stages) == 0) {
		$Due['reason'] = __('Nothing overdue');
		return $Due;
	}
	$Target = null;
	foreach ($Stages as $Stage) {
		if ($Position['maxdays'] >= $Stage['daysoverdue']) {
			$Target = $Stage;
		}
	}
	if ($Target === null) {
		$Due['reason'] = __('Not overdue enough for the first stage');
		return $Due;
	}
	/* letters sent since the oldest currently-overdue item fell due belong to this run of overdue invoices */
	$CycleStart = date('Y-m-d', strtotime('-' . (int)$Position['maxdays'] . ' days', strtotime($AsAt)));
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(stage), 0), MAX(sentdate)
						FROM dunninglog
						WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "' AND sentdate >= '" . $CycleStart . "'");
	$Last = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	if ($Last[0] >= $Target['stage']) {
		$Due['reason'] = __('Stage already sent') . ' (' . $Target['stage'] . ')';
		return $Due;
	}
	$MinDays = isset($_SESSION['CreditDunningMinDays']) ? (int)$_SESSION['CreditDunningMinDays'] : 14;
	if ($Last[1] != '' and strtotime($Last[1]) > strtotime('-' . $MinDays . ' days', strtotime($AsAt . ' 23:59:59'))) {
		$Due['reason'] = __('A letter was sent less than') . ' ' . $MinDays . ' ' . __('days ago');
		return $Due;
	}
	$Due['stage'] = $Target;
	return $Due;
}

/* Email addresses of the customer's accounts contacts (the contacts flagged to receive statements) */
function CreditAccountsEmails($DebtorNo) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT email FROM custcontacts WHERE statement = 1 AND debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'");
	$Emails = array();
	while ($MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result)) {
		if (IsEmailAddress($MyRow[0])) {
			$Emails[] = $MyRow[0];
		}
	}
	return $Emails;
}

/* Build the letter for a customer at a stage. Placeholders: [CUSTOMER] [CURRENCY] [AMOUNT] [INVOICES] [COMPANY] [DATE]
 * Returns array(subject, body) as plain text. */
function CreditBuildLetter($Stage, $Customer, $Items, $Amount) {
	$DP = $Customer['decimalplaces'];
	$Lines = '';
	foreach ($Items as $Item) {
		$Lines .= html_entity_decode(__($Item['typename']), ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') . ' ' . $Item['transno'] . '  ' . __('dated') . ' ' . ConvertSQLDate($Item['trandate']) .
				'  ' . __('due') . ' ' . ConvertSQLDate($Item['duedate']) . '  ' . $Customer['currcode'] . ' ' . locale_number_format($Item['balance'], $DP) . "\n";
	}
	$Replace = array('[CUSTOMER]' => html_entity_decode($Customer['name'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'),
					'[CURRENCY]' => $Customer['currcode'],
					'[AMOUNT]' => locale_number_format($Amount, $DP),
					'[INVOICES]' => rtrim($Lines),
					'[COMPANY]' => html_entity_decode($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['coyname'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'),
					'[DATE]' => date($_SESSION['DefaultDateFormat']));
	$Subject = strtr(html_entity_decode($Stage['subject'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'), $Replace);
	$Body = strtr(html_entity_decode($Stage['body'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'), $Replace);
	return array($Subject, $Body);
}

/* Overdue items with the transaction type name, for letters (same selection as CreditOverdueItems) */
function CreditOverdueItemsForLetter($DebtorNo, $AsAt) {
	$Items = CreditOverdueItems($DebtorNo, $AsAt);
	foreach ($Items as $Key => $Item) {
		$Result = DB_query("SELECT typename FROM systypes WHERE typeid = '" . $Item['type'] . "'");
		$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
		$Items[$Key]['typename'] = $MyRow[0];
	}
	return $Items;
}

/* Post a customer transaction of one of the credit control types (charge, waiver, write-off): the debtortrans row and, when
 * debtors are linked to the GL, the balanced gltrans entries.
 *
 *   $CustAmount  signed amount in the customer's currency (positive debits the customer, negative credits)
 *   $HomeAmount  the same amount in the company's currency, at the rate the customer items it relates to were posted at
 *   $GLLines     array of account => signed home amount for everything except debtors control; the debtors control entry
 *                is derived so that the journal always balances
 *
 * The caller is responsible for the transaction. Returns array('id' => debtortrans id, 'transno' => number). */
function CreditPostTransaction($Type, $DebtorNo, $CustAmount, $HomeAmount, $Reference, $GLLines, $Narrative) {
	if (!function_exists('GetNextTransNo')) {
		include_once(__DIR__ . '/SQL_CommonFunctions.php');
	}
	$TransNo = GetNextTransNo($Type);
	$TranDate = date($_SESSION['DefaultDateFormat']);
	$PeriodNo = GetPeriod($TranDate);
	$SQLDate = FormatDateForSQL($TranDate);
	$DP = $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['decimalplaces'];
	$HomeAmount = round($HomeAmount, $DP);
	$Rate = ($HomeAmount != 0 ? $CustAmount / $HomeAmount : 1);

	$Result = DB_query("SELECT branchcode, salesman FROM custbranch WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "' ORDER BY branchcode LIMIT 1");
	$Branch = DB_fetch_array($Result);

	$SQL = "INSERT INTO debtortrans (transno,
									type,
									debtorno,
									branchcode,
									trandate,
									inputdate,
									prd,
									reference,
									tpe,
									rate,
									ovamount,
									invtext,
									salesperson)
			SELECT '" . $TransNo . "',
					'" . $Type . "',
					'" . $DebtorNo . "',
					'" . ($Branch ? $Branch['branchcode'] : '') . "',
					'" . $SQLDate . "',
					NOW(),
					'" . $PeriodNo . "',
					'" . DB_escape_string(mb_substr($Reference, 0, 50)) . "',
					salestype,
					'" . $Rate . "',
					'" . $CustAmount . "',
					'" . DB_escape_string($Narrative) . "',
					'" . ($Branch ? $Branch['salesman'] : '') . "'
			FROM debtorsmaster
			WHERE debtorno = '" . $DebtorNo . "'";
	DB_query($SQL, __('The customer transaction could not be posted because'));
	$ID = DB_Last_Insert_ID('debtortrans', 'id');

	if ($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['gllink_debtors'] == 1) {
		$Total = 0;
		foreach ($GLLines as $Account => $Amount) {
			$Amount = round($Amount, $DP);
			$Total += $Amount;
			DB_query("INSERT INTO gltrans (type, typeno, trandate, periodno, account, narrative, amount)
					VALUES ('" . $Type . "', '" . $TransNo . "', '" . $SQLDate . "', '" . $PeriodNo . "', '" . $Account . "',
							'" . DB_escape_string(mb_substr($Narrative, 0, 200)) . "', '" . $Amount . "')",
					__('The GL entry could not be posted because'));
		}
		DB_query("INSERT INTO gltrans (type, typeno, trandate, periodno, account, narrative, amount)
				VALUES ('" . $Type . "', '" . $TransNo . "', '" . $SQLDate . "', '" . $PeriodNo . "', '" . $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['debtorsact'] . "',
						'" . DB_escape_string(mb_substr($Narrative, 0, 200)) . "', '" . -$Total . "')",
				__('The debtors control entry could not be posted because'));
	}
	return array('id' => $ID, 'transno' => $TransNo, 'homeamount' => $HomeAmount);
}

/* Record that a credit (negative) transaction settles part or all of a positive one, the way the allocation screen does. */
function CreditAllocate($CreditID, $DebitID, $Amount) {
	DB_query("INSERT INTO custallocns (amt, datealloc, transid_allocfrom, transid_allocto)
			VALUES ('" . $Amount . "', CURRENT_DATE, '" . $CreditID . "', '" . $DebitID . "')");
	DB_query("UPDATE debtortrans SET alloc = alloc + " . $Amount . ",
									settled = IF(ABS(ovamount + ovgst + ovfreight + ovdiscount - alloc) < 0.005, 1, 0)
			WHERE id = '" . $DebitID . "'");
	DB_query("UPDATE debtortrans SET alloc = alloc - " . $Amount . ",
									settled = IF(ABS(ovamount + ovgst + ovfreight + ovdiscount - alloc) < 0.005, 1, 0)
			WHERE id = '" . $CreditID . "'");
}

/* Check that a GL account chosen in the settings exists; used before anything is posted */
function CreditGLAccountReady($ConfName) {
	if ($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['gllink_debtors'] != 1) {
		return true;
	}
	if (!isset($_SESSION[$ConfName]) or $_SESSION[$ConfName] === '') {
		return false;
	}
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM chartmaster WHERE accountcode = '" . $_SESSION[$ConfName] . "'");
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return $MyRow[0] == 1;
}

function CreditSettingsLink() {
	global $RootPath;
	return '<a href="' . $RootPath . '/CreditControlSettings.php">' . __('Credit Control Settings') . '</a>';
}
